title: Smallest prime after 211 failing the Erdos 1059 property

problemStatement.formal: AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite(n) := \forall k, k! < n \to \neg\operatorname{Prime}(n-k!);\ 223\text{ is prime},\ \neg AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite(223),\text{ and no prime lies strictly between }211\text{ and }223.
problemStatement.plain: Identify the first prime after 211 that fails the Erdos 1059 factorial-subtraction property. The Lean proof shows 223 is prime, that 223 - 4! = 199 is prime, and that there are no intervening primes between 211 and 223.
whyMatters: The result turns a computational search target into a small certified witness.
It records both the primality gap after 211 and the specific factorial subtraction that breaks the property.
The file is a good example of using Lean's decidable arithmetic for exact finite number-theory checks.

proven: `AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite` defines the factorial-subtraction property for a natural number.
`prime_223`, `prime_199`, and `next_prime_after_211` certify the local prime facts around 211 and 223.
`counterexample_223` proves that 223 fails the property because 223 - 4! = 199 is prime.
`smallest_failing_prime_after_211` packages the computation as the first failing prime after 211.
open: `Erdos1059OQ03.lean` itself has zero axioms and zero sorries; broader density and infinitude claims in sibling Erdos 1059 files are axiom-backed.
knownResults.goal: Expose the verified finite witness and avoid implying that the wider Erdos 1059 density program is settled here.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: p = 223 is the smallest prime > 211 failing the property (223-24=199 is prime). All results verified by decide. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
builtItems: Created Proofs/Erdos1059OQ03.lean: 47 lines, 5 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries
insights: 223 is the very next prime after 211 — there are no primes in (211, 223)
Also 223 - 120 = 103 is prime (a second failure), but 4! suffices
The Erdős 1059 property is rare — even the next prime after a witness fails
